backfill_note: The run directory was authored on 2026-08-06 from the firsthand notes taken during the original 2026-06-26 experiment (firsthand-benchmark.md). The recorded behaviors are the outputs observed then. The original ad-hoc harness scripts and the downloaded coreutils binary were removed by the post-publish cleanup policy, so this run.sh is a RECONSTRUCTED harness: it recreates the exact fixtures and re-runs the same commands against pinned Microsoft Coreutils 2026.6.16 so a third party can reproduce the behavior matrix. It was not re-executed at authoring time; treat results.json as the 2026-06-26 observation, and run.sh as the way to re-confirm it.

environment.runner: native Windows shells (cmd.exe + PowerShell + Git Bash), no Docker
environment.note: This is a CLI behavior / dialect-dispatch study, not a timing benchmark. The one timing observation (experiment 8) is explicitly approximate and is NOT presented as a performance win; hardware specs are therefore omitted.

subject.name: Microsoft Coreutils for Windows
subject.install: winget install --version 2026.6.16 Microsoft.Coreutils   (original run used the portable GitHub release zip because winget needs UAC elevation, unavailable to the unattended session)

baselines.name: PowerShell aliases
baselines.note: sort->Sort-Object, ls->Get-ChildItem, etc. shadow external exes.

cited_not_measured.gnu_test_suite_compat: uutils GNU test-suite pass rate (0.8.0 ~94.7%, 0.9.0 ~90.6%) is a LINUX figure, not Windows end-to-end. The post never claims 'N% identical to GNU on Windows'.
cited_not_measured.install_integration: hardlink creation + PowerShell-profile integration + settings-in-registry are reported by Microsoft docs. The unattended run used argv0 shim copies (behavior-equivalent) and did NOT install, so PATH/registry/profile integration is cited, not measured.

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: tools discarded post-publish per firsthand cleanup rules (coreutils.exe, the release zip, shim copies, big.txt fixture). No large raw dumps were kept.
raw_artifacts.note: run.sh regenerates every fixture deterministically (tiny) and the big-file perf fixture on demand (never committed). The deterministic evidence — the behavior matrix in results.json — is committed.
